post.title: 9 states don't tax wages. Here's how they pay the bills
post.ig:
9 states don't tax your paycheck. So who pays the bills?
As of 2026, Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas and Wyoming have no income tax; Washington taxes only some capital gains (its new tax on income over $1 million starts in 2028).
Tennessee's average combined sales tax was 9.61% as of July 2026, vs a 7.53% population-weighted US average. In Texas, sales tax was 58% of state tax collections in fiscal 2025.
Alaska has no state sales tax and leans on oil and its Permanent Fund, which paid each eligible resident $1,200 in 2026 ($1,000 dividend plus $200 one-time energy relief). Chart amounts include one-time relief in 2022, 2024 and 2026.
Rough math: $40,000 of taxable spending is $3,844 in sales tax at 9.61% vs $3,012 at 7.53%. Simplified: actual rates vary by city, and some items like groceries are taxed differently.
Sources: Tax Foundation (Feb and July 2026), Texas Comptroller (FY2025), Alaska Dept. of Revenue (2026), NH Dept. of Revenue Administration.
News and education, not financial advice.
